draft_context.source_title: Enhancing CA Practices: Key Updates in Mozilla Root Store Policy, v3.0
draft_context.description: Mozilla remains committed to fostering a secure, agile, and transparent Web PKI ecosystem. The new Mozilla Root Store Policy (MRSP) v3.0 , effective March 15, 2025, introduces critical updates to strengthen Certificate Authority (CA) practices and enhance compliance. A major focus of MRSP v3.0 is tackling the long-standing challenge of delayed certificate revocation —an issue that has historically weakened the security and reliability of TLS certificate management. The updated policy establishes clearer revocation expectations, improved incident reporting, subscriber education by CAs, revocation planning, and automated certificate issuance to ensure that certificate replacement and revocation can be handled promptly and at scale. Beyond improving revocation, MRSP v3.0 also introduces policies to move CA operators toward dedicated hierarchies for TLS and S/MIME certificates and to enhance CA private key security with improved lifecycle tracking. All of these updates raise the bar for CA operations, reinforcing security and trust across the broader internet ecosystem . Addressing Delayed Certificate Revocation One of the most persistent challenges in certificate management has been ensuring that TLS server certificates are revoked quickly when necessary. Many website operators struggle to replace certificates efficiently, while security advocates emphasize the need for rapid revocation and automated certificate lifecycle management to reduce risks. To strike the right balance between security, stability, and operational feasibility, MRSP v3.0 introduces several key changes towards clearer and more comprehensive revocation expectations . No Exceptions to Revocation Requirements Previously, some CA operators expressed uncertainty about whether Mozilla could grant exceptions to revocation timelines in certain situations. MRSP v3.0 explicitly reiterates that Mozilla does not grant exceptions to the TLS Baseline Requirements for revocation . This will promote more consistent enforcement of revocation policy. Stronger Subscriber Communication and Contractual Clarity CA operators must proactively warn subscribers about the risks of relying on publicly trusted certificates in environments that cannot tolerate timely revocation. Additionally, Subscriber Agreements must explicitly require cooperation with revocation timelines, ensuring CA operators can act without unnecessary delays . Mass Revocation Preparedness Historically, large-scale certificate revocations have been challenging, leading to operational slowdowns, and ecosystem-wide risks when urgent action is required. To prevent revocation delays, MRSP v3.0 mandates mass revocation readiness to help ensure that CA operators proactively plan for such scenarios. CA operators will be required to develop, maintain, and test comprehensive plans to revoke large numbers of certificates quickly when necessary. And, to further strengthen mass revocation preparedness, MRSP v3.0 introduces a third-party assessment requirement. Assessors will verify that CA operators: Maintain well-documented, actionable plans for large-scale revocation, Demonstrate feasibility through regular testing, and Continuously improve their approach based on lessons learned. These measures ensure CA operators are fully prepared for high-impact security events . By strengthening mass revocation preparedness–and investing in CRLite–Mozilla is working to make certificate revocation a reliable security control. Enhancing Automation in Certificate Issuance and Renewal Automation plays a critical role in ensuring certificates can be replaced in a timely manner. To further encourage adoption of automation, MRSP v3.0 introduces new requirements for CA operators seeking root inclusion with the “websites” trust bit enabled, including: offering automation options for Domain Control Validation (DCV), certificate issuance, and renewal (demonstrated by a publicly accessible test website demonstrating automated certificate replacement at least every 30 days). Test website details must be disclosed in the Common CA Database (CCADB) , adding transparency to this requirement. This push for more automation aligns with industry best practices , reducing reliance on manual processes, improving security, and minimizing mismanagement risks. Phasing Out Dual-Purpose (TLS and S/MIME) Root CAs A significant change introduced in MRSP v3.0 is the phase-out of dual-purpose root CAs—those with both the “websites” trust bit and the “email” trust bit enabled. The industry is already moving toward separating TLS and S/MIME hierarchies due to their distinct security needs. Keeping these uses separate at the root certificate level ensures more focused compliance, increases CA agility, reduces complexity, and enhances security. Going forward, Mozilla’s Root Store will require that new root CA certificates are dedicated to either TLS or S/MIME, and CA operators with existing dual-purpose roots will need to submit a transition plan to Mozilla by April 15, 2026, and complete a full migration to separate roots by December 31, 2028. This move enhances clarity and security by ensuring TLS and S/MIME compliance requirements remain distinct and enforceable. Strengthening CA Key Security with “Cradle-to-Grave” Monitoring Another major enhancement in MRSP v3.0 is the introduction of stricter key lifecycle monitoring to protect “parked” CA private keys. A “parked” key is a private key that the CA operator has generated for future use, but not yet used in a CA certificate . MRSP v3.0 adds mandatory reporting of parked key public hashes (corresponding to the parked CA private key) in annual audits. By enforcing transparency and accountability, Mozilla strengthens protections against undetected key compromise or misuse. Conclusion MRSP v3.0 represents a major step forward in ensuring stronger CA accountability with more reliable certificate revocation processes, better automation and operational resilience, and enhanced security for CA private keys. In all, these changes help modernize the Web PKI and ensure that CA operations will remain transparent, accountable, and secure. We encourage you to engage with the Mozilla community and to contribute to these efforts and our shared mission of ensuring a secure and trustworthy online experience for all users . The post Enhancing CA Practices: Key Updates in Mozilla Root Store Policy, v3.0 appeared first on Mozilla Security Blog .
paragraphs: Mozilla remains committed to fostering a secure, agile, and transparent Web PKI ecosystem. The new Mozilla Root Store Policy (MRSP) v3.0 , effective March 15, 2025, introduces critical updates to strengthen Certificate Authority (CA) practices and enhance compliance.

A major focus of MRSP v3.0 is tackling the long-standing challenge of delayed certificate revocation —an issue that has historically weakened the security and reliability of TLS certificate management. The updated policy establishes clearer revocation expectations, improved incident reporting, subscriber education by CAs, revocation planning, and automated certificate issuance to ensure that certificate replacement and revocation can be handled promptly and at scale.

Beyond improving revocation, MRSP v3.0 also introduces policies to move CA operators toward dedicated hierarchies for TLS and S/MIME certificates and to enhance CA private key security with improved lifecycle tracking. All of these updates raise the bar for CA operations, reinforcing security and trust across the broader internet ecosystem .
To strike the right balance between security, stability, and operational feasibility, MRSP v3.0 introduces several key changes towards clearer and more comprehensive revocation expectations .

Previously, some CA operators expressed uncertainty about whether Mozilla could grant exceptions to revocation timelines in certain situations. MRSP v3.0 explicitly reiterates that Mozilla does not grant exceptions to the TLS Baseline Requirements for revocation . This will promote more consistent enforcement of revocation policy.

article.title: Benchmarking Secure-and-Functional Remediation and How Snyk Agent Fix Lifts Frontier-Model Fix Rates by over 14%
article.summary: We benchmarked how well leading models produce vulnerability fixes that are both secure and functional, across ~150 real vulnerable code samples in JavaScript, Java, and Python. We ran each model on its own and with Snyk Intelligence (the new agentic Agent Fix architecture).

sections.body: We benchmarked how well leading models produce vulnerability fixes that are both secure and functional, across ~150 real vulnerable code samples in JavaScript, Java, and Python. sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: Out-of-the-box frontier models cluster at 72–75%. Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Opus 4.6 all land within a few points of each other. On secure-and-functional fixing, model choice barely moves the number.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: Snyk Intelligence moves the same models clear of that cluster. Opus 4.6 rises from 74.6% to 85.4% , a 10.8-point gain ( 14.48% more samples fixed). The variable is the security context, not the model.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now
sections.body: The lift is largest where the model is weakest. Opus alone fixes only 64% of Python samples; with Snyk Intelligence, that reaches 88%.

sections.heading: What to watch next
sections.body: Coding-agent benchmarks exist for unit-test generation, SWE-bench-style bug fixing, and code completion. There is no widely used public benchmark for the task a security team actually cares about: take code with a known vulnerability and produce a fix that removes the vulnerability and keeps the code working. Those are two independent bars, and clearing one while failing the other is a common, expensive failure mode. A fix that removes a SQL injection but changes what the query returns has not helped anyone. A fix that looks clean but leaves the injection in place is worse, because it reads like a solution.

draft_context.description: A benchmark of secure, functional vulnerability fixes across JavaScript, Java, and Python shows Snyk Intelligence helps frontier models break past a 72–75% performance plateau.
paragraphs: We benchmarked how well leading models produce vulnerability fixes that are both secure and functional, across ~150 real vulnerable code samples in JavaScript, Java, and Python. We ran each model on its own and with Snyk Intelligence (the new agentic Agent Fix architecture). The headline findings:

Out-of-the-box frontier models cluster at 72–75%. Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Opus 4.6 all land within a few points of each other. On secure-and-functional fixing, model choice barely moves the number.

Snyk Intelligence moves the same models clear of that cluster. Opus 4.6 rises from 74.6% to 85.4% , a 10.8-point gain ( 14.48% more samples fixed). The variable is the security context, not the model.
The lift is largest where the model is weakest. Opus alone fixes only 64% of Python samples; with Snyk Intelligence, that reaches 88%.

Coding-agent benchmarks exist for unit-test generation, SWE-bench-style bug fixing, and code completion. There is no widely used public benchmark for the task a security team actually cares about: take code with a known vulnerability and produce a fix that removes the vulnerability and keeps the code working. Those are two independent bars, and clearing one while failing the other is a common, expensive failure mode. A fix that removes a SQL injection but changes what the query returns has not helped anyone. A fix that looks clean but leaves the injection in place is worse, because it reads like a solution.

So we built a benchmark that scores both bars on every fix, and ran frontier models through it twice: on their own, and equipped with Snyk's security intelligence . The question we wanted answered in plain terms: how much does Snyk's security context change what a frontier model can fix, and where?

article.title: Transformers Explained Visually
article.summary: Fundamentally, text-generative Transformer models operate on the principle of next-token prediction : given a text prompt from the user, what is the most probable next token (a word or part of a word) that will follow this input? The core innovation and power of Transformers lie in their use of self-attention mechanism, which allows them to process entire sequences and capture long-range dependencies more effectively than previous architectures.

article.title: Vì sao màn hình TV 4K không hiển thị sắc nét như mong đợi?
article.summary: Có nhiều nguyên nhân khiến TV 4K không hiển thị đúng chất lượng siêu nét. Nguyên nhân phổ biến nhất là phần lớn nội dung video hiện nay chưa đạt chuẩn 4K nguyên bản, buộc TV phải kích hoạt thuật toán nâng cấp độ phân giải (upscaling) để lấp đầy các điểm ảnh dư thừa.
article.dek: Có nhiều nguyên nhân khiến TV 4K không hiển thị đúng chất lượng siêu nét.
article.hook: Nguyên nhân phổ biến nhất là phần lớn nội dung video hiện nay chưa đạt chuẩn 4K nguyên bản, buộc TV phải kích hoạt thuật toán nâng cấp độ phân giải (upscaling) để lấp đầy các điểm ảnh dư thừa.

sections.heading: Bối cảnh: điều gì đang đổi
sections.body: Có nhiều nguyên nhân khiến TV 4K không hiển thị đúng chất lượng siêu nét.

sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: Nguyên nhân phổ biến nhất là phần lớn nội dung video hiện nay chưa đạt chuẩn 4K nguyên bản, buộc TV phải kích hoạt thuật toán nâng cấp độ phân giải (upscaling) để lấp đầy các điểm ảnh dư thừa. Bên cạnh đó, các dịch vụ trực tuyến thường tự động hạ chất lượng xuống dưới mức 2.160p khi mạng chập chờn, hoặc nén dữ liệu rất nặng với băng thông chỉ khoảng 15 - 25 Mbps, tạo ra khoảng cách chất lượng rất xa so với mức 108 - 128 Mbps của đĩa 4K Blu-ray.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Về mặt kết nối, các thiết bị ngoại vi như Apple TV 4K hay TV Box có thể đang xuất nhầm tín hiệu 1.080p, trong khi dây cáp HDMI chuẩn cũ cũng tạo thành nút thắt cổ chai giới hạn chất lượng. Để truyền tải đầy đủ tín hiệu 4K với tần số quét cao và HDR, người dùng cần tối thiểu cáp chuẩn HDMI 2.0 hoặc 2.1 thay vì chuẩn HDMI 1.4.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Ngoài ra, các hệ máy chơi game console như PlayStation 5 hay Xbox Series X cũng thường hạ độ phân giải dựng hình xuống rồi áp dụng kỹ thuật tái tạo để duy trì tốc độ khung hình.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Các tính năng xử lý hậu kỳ tích hợp trên TV cũng có thể phản tác dụng nếu bị can thiệp quá mức. Bộ lọc giảm nhiễu hoặc làm mịn dải màu quá đà sẽ xóa đi hạt điện ảnh và chi tiết tự nhiên, khiến làn da nhân vật trông như tượng sáp, trong khi thanh độ sắc nét (sharpness) đẩy lên quá cao sẽ làm hình ảnh bị gai góc bất thường. Đồng thời, độ trễ phản hồi điểm ảnh của tấm nền LCD hoặc cơ chế chuyển khung hình của OLED cũng có thể làm nhòe mờ chi tiết trong các cảnh chuyển động nhanh.

article.title: Gmail đã có tính năng được chờ đợi suốt nhiều năm
article.summary: Tính năng mới đang được Google triển khai đến người dùng Gmail trên Android lẫn iOS. Khi nhận được email chứa mã xác minh từ các dịch vụ như ngân hàng hay cửa hàng trực tuyến, một nút sẽ xuất hiện bên dưới dòng tiêu đề, tương tự như cách hiển thị bản xem trước hình ảnh hoặc tài liệu đính kèm.

sections.heading: Bối cảnh: điều gì đang đổi
sections.body: Tính năng mới đang được Google triển khai đến người dùng Gmail trên Android lẫn iOS.

sections.body: Khi nhận được email chứa mã xác minh từ các dịch vụ như ngân hàng hay cửa hàng trực tuyến, một nút sẽ xuất hiện bên dưới dòng tiêu đề, tương tự như cách hiển thị bản xem trước hình ảnh hoặc tài liệu đính kèm.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Cách hoạt động của nút này rất đơn giản: nó sẽ hiển thị nội dung như "Copy code: xxxxxx". Người dùng chỉ cần chạm vào nút, mã sẽ được lưu vào bộ nhớ tạm của điện thoại, sẵn sàng để dán vào ứng dụng hoặc trang web yêu cầu.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Mặc dù đây không phải là một thay đổi mang tính cách mạng của Gmail, nhưng việc giảm thiểu thao tác luôn là điều tích cực, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh các vụ lừa đảo ngày càng gia tăng khiến xác thực hai yếu tố (2FA) trở nên cần thiết hơn bao giờ hết.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Trước đây, người dùng Gmail phải mở email, tìm mã giữa các dòng chữ, cẩn thận chọn để không sao chép thêm khoảng trắng trước khi quay lại ứng dụng để dán. Giờ đây, với tính năng mới này, quy trình trở nên nhanh chóng và dễ dàng hơn nhiều.

Khi nhận được email chứa mã xác minh từ các dịch vụ như ngân hàng hay cửa hàng trực tuyến, một nút sẽ xuất hiện bên dưới dòng tiêu đề, tương tự như cách hiển thị bản xem trước hình ảnh hoặc tài liệu đính kèm.

Cách hoạt động của nút này rất đơn giản: nó sẽ hiển thị nội dung như "Copy code: xxxxxx". Người dùng chỉ cần chạm vào nút, mã sẽ được lưu vào bộ nhớ tạm của điện thoại, sẵn sàng để dán vào ứng dụng hoặc trang web yêu cầu.

Mặc dù đây không phải là một thay đổi mang tính cách mạng của Gmail, nhưng việc giảm thiểu thao tác luôn là điều tích cực, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh các vụ lừa đảo ngày càng gia tăng khiến xác thực hai yếu tố (2FA) trở nên cần thiết hơn bao giờ hết.

Trước đây, người dùng Gmail phải mở email, tìm mã giữa các dòng chữ, cẩn thận chọn để không sao chép thêm khoảng trắng trước khi quay lại ứng dụng để dán. Giờ đây, với tính năng mới này, quy trình trở nên nhanh chóng và dễ dàng hơn nhiều.

Hiện tại, tính năng này chỉ có sẵn trên ứng dụng di động, cả trên Android (từ phiên bản 2026.09.07) và iOS (từ phiên bản 6.0.260907), trong khi vẫn chưa thấy nút này xuất hiện trên phiên bản máy tính. Hy vọng trong tương lai, nút sao chép mã sẽ được tích hợp trực tiếp trong thông báo Gmail trên Android nhằm giúp người dùng tiết kiệm thời gian hơn nữa khi cần nhập mã xác thực.

article.title: Màn hình máy tính trang bị nhiều cổng USB dùng để làm gì?
article.summary: Các mẫu màn hình hiện đại có thể đi kèm nhiều cổng USB khác nhau. Cách thức hoạt động của các cổng USB trên màn hình phụ thuộc vào từng mẫu.
article.dek: Các mẫu màn hình hiện đại có thể đi kèm nhiều cổng USB khác nhau.
article.hook: Một số màn hình có kết nối video và hub USB tách biệt, yêu cầu người dùng sử dụng cáp HDMI hoặc DisplayPort cho hình ảnh và một cáp USB riêng để kết nối với máy tính.

sections.heading: Bối cảnh: điều gì đang đổi
sections.body: Các mẫu màn hình hiện đại có thể đi kèm nhiều cổng USB khác nhau.

sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: Cách thức hoạt động của các cổng USB trên màn hình phụ thuộc vào từng mẫu. Một số màn hình có kết nối video và hub USB tách biệt, yêu cầu người dùng sử dụng cáp HDMI hoặc DisplayPort cho hình ảnh và một cáp USB riêng để kết nối với máy tính.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Đặc biệt, các màn hình hỗ trợ USB-C cho phép cáp duy nhất thực hiện cả hai chức năng: truyền hình ảnh và dữ liệu, tiện lợi cho nhu cầu công việc.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Với những màn hình tích hợp hub USB thường có hai loại cổng: upstream (kết nối với máy tính) và downstream (kết nối với thiết bị ngoại vi). Tuy nhiên, không có quy tắc nào quy định rằng màn hình phải có một cổng upstream và một cổng downstream. paragraphs: Các mẫu màn hình hiện đại có thể đi kèm nhiều cổng USB khác nhau

Cách thức hoạt động của các cổng USB trên màn hình phụ thuộc vào từng mẫu. Một số màn hình có kết nối video và hub USB tách biệt, yêu cầu người dùng sử dụng cáp HDMI hoặc DisplayPort cho hình ảnh và một cáp USB riêng để kết nối với máy tính.
Đặc biệt, các màn hình hỗ trợ USB-C cho phép cáp duy nhất thực hiện cả hai chức năng: truyền hình ảnh và dữ liệu, tiện lợi cho nhu cầu công việc.

Với những màn hình tích hợp hub USB thường có hai loại cổng: upstream (kết nối với máy tính) và downstream (kết nối với thiết bị ngoại vi). Tuy nhiên, không có quy tắc nào quy định rằng màn hình phải có một cổng upstream và một cổng downstream. Một số mẫu có thể có nhiều cổng USB-A downstream và một cổng USB-B upstream, trong khi các mẫu khác có thể sử dụng USB-C cho upstream.

Do đó, các cổng USB trên màn hình thường phù hợp cho việc kết nối các thiết bị không yêu cầu tốc độ cao, như bàn phím và chuột.

Ngoài ra, một số cổng USB trên màn hình còn có khả năng sạc thiết bị. Tuy nhiên, việc này phụ thuộc vào từng mẫu màn hình và cài đặt của nó. Ví dụ, một số màn hình Dell có chế độ "Other USB Charging", cho phép các cổng USB vẫn cung cấp điện khi màn hình ở chế độ chờ.

The three bugs in question are tracked as CVE-2025-39682 (severity score 9.8/10 - critical), CVE-2026-53266 (severity score 8.8/10 - high), and CVE-2025-39964 (severity score 7.8/10 - high). All three have already been patched in the Linux kernel. CVE-2025-39682 was fixed in stable releases 6.1.149, 6.6.103, 6.12.44 and 6.16.4, while CVE-2025-39964 was fixed in 5.10.245, 5.15.194, 6.1.154, 6.6.108, 6.12.49 and 6.16.9. CVE-2026-53266 has been fixed upstream and backported to supported stable/distribution kernel branches, including 5.10.259, 6.1.176 and 6.12.94. The first issue is an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive patch which could allow unauthenticated threat actors to launch memory disclosure or denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. The second one (CVE-2026-53266) is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ebtables Source Network Address Translation (SNAT) Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) rewrite patch which allows local attackers to escalate privileges or mount DoS attacks. The last one (CVE-2025-39964) is a race condition flaw that allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket, which allows local malicious actors to crash the system or corrupt cryptographic operation results, leading to data integrity issues and possible DoS states. Attacks in the wild Red Hat acknowledged that all three are being abused in real-life attacks. “This CVE is high risk and there are known public exploits leveraging this vulnerability. Address this vulnerability with high priority,” it said in all three advisories. However, there are no details as to who is currently using these exploits, against whom, and to what cause. There are currently no separate reports of cyberattacks referencing any of the abovementioned vulnerabilities. However, CISA still reacted. All three flaws were added on September 18, 2026, and all three have a small three-day deadline for patching that expires on September 21. Usually, CISA would grant Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies a three-week deadline to patch up, with just exceptionally dangerous flaws getting a shorter window. That being said, these flaws are likely extremely dangerous. In theory... In a hypothetical scenario, a threat actor could target a Linux system using kernel TLS (kTLS) by sending a specially-crafted TLS record that triggers CVE-2025-39682 and causing either a crash, or even arbitrary code execution. Attackers that already have a low privilege foothold on the target endpoint could use CVE_2025-39964 to escalate privileges, while on systems using the affected bridge/netfilter configuration, CVE-2026-53266 could be used for privilege escalation, as well. According to the Red Hat advisory, there is a chance that CVE-2025-39682 is remotely triggerable, but only when the system is using the affected kTLS receive path. The other two flaws are exclusively local vulnerabilities. Besides fixes, two out of the three flaws also have possible mitigations. For the improper check one, users should prevent module tls from being loaded. For the out-of-bounds write one, users are advised to disable ARP hardware address rewriting in ebtables SNAT rules, or remove ebtables SNAT rules that operate on ARP traffic on bridge interfaces. The final vulnerability, currently does not have a working mitigation, and the only way to stay secure is to apply the provided patches. Linux kernel vulnerabilities are generally considered serious, but the severity still depends on the flaw and how the affected kernel is deployed. Earlier this year, security researchers disclosed four local privilege escalation flaws, called DirtyAH6 (CVE-2026-80844), TUNderflow (CVE-2026-81000), PPPoEject (CVE-2026-68121), and DiagSpill (CVE-2026-74469). article.title: pgsql-test: Real Postgres Testing for Faster Development Loops
article.summary: Application code has fast testing loops: runners, fixtures, and red-green feedback in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python. Postgres can be tested too, but database logic often sits outside those loops.
article.dek: Application code has fast testing loops: runners, fixtures, and red-green feedback in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python.
article.hook: Application code has fast testing loops: runners, fixtures, and red-green feedback in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python.

sections.heading: Context: what is changing
sections.body: Application code has fast testing loops: runners, fixtures, and red-green feedback in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python. Postgres can be tested too, but database logic often sits outside those loops. Developers have to provision state, manage transactions, or fall back to a pasted query, a browser refresh, or a manual check. That gap shapes architecture. When rules are easier to test in application code than in Postgres, they tend to end up there, even when Postgres is the better place to enforce them.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: Mocks do not close the gap. They test how application code handles a result, not whether Postgres will produce it. A mock does not exercise a foreign key, fire a trigger, evaluate a row-level security policy, or verify the database role under which a query actually runs.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: pgsql-test is an MIT-licensed harness that puts a real PostgreSQL database inside those loops. It spins up an ephemeral PostgreSQL database, seeds it once, and rolls every test back to that seeded state. Assertions run in the project’s existing test runner, and Postgres executes the constraints, functions, and policies under test. It is not the first way to test Postgres—pgTAP has long done it in pure SQL. pgsql-test targets the application layer instead, where most developers already work.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now
sections.body: Row-level security (RLS) makes access rules enforceable by Postgres. Policies are pure database logic, invisible to mocks, and a wrong one can leak rows. Testing them means checking both what a user can access and what they cannot.

sections.heading: What to watch next
sections.body: The pgsql-test harness provides an administrative client, pg , for setup and an application client, db , for testing grants and policies. Superusers bypass RLS, so tests need to exercise the database roles and permissions the application actually uses.

draft_context.description: Application code has fast testing loops: runners, fixtures, and red-green feedback in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python. Postgres can be tested too, but database logic often sits outside those loops. When rules are easier to test in application code than in Postgres, they tend to end up there, even when Postgres is the better place to enforce them. Mocks do not close the gap. They test how application code handles a result, not whether Postgres will produce it. A mock does not exercise a foreign key, fire a trigger, evaluate a row-level security policy, or verify the database role under which a query actually runs. pgsql-test is an MIT-licensed harness that puts a real PostgreSQL database inside those loops. It spins up an ephemeral PostgreSQL database, seeds it once, and rolls every test back to that seeded state. Assertions run in the project’s existing test runner, and Postgres executes the constraints, functions, and policies under test. It is not the first way to test Postgres—pgTAP has long done it in pure SQL. pgsql-test targets the application layer instead, where most developers already work. Testing row-level security Row-level security (RLS) makes access rules enforceable by Postgres. Policies are pure database logic, invisible to mocks, and a wrong one can leak rows. Testing them means checking both what a user can access and what they cannot. The pgsql-test harness provides an administrative client, pg , for setup and an application client, db , for testing grants and policies. Superusers bypass RLS, so tests need to exercise the database roles and permissions the application actually uses. Suppose a project defines app.documents with an ownership policy, and its fixtures insert document 101 owned by Alice and document 202 owned by Bob. Each test runs inside a transaction that is rolled back afterwards, so every test starts from the seeded state: import { getConnections } from 'pgsql-test'; let db, teardown; beforeAll(async () => { // create a fresh database and deploy the project's schema ({ db, teardown } = await getConnections()); }); afterAll(() => teardown()); beforeEach(() => db.beforeEach()); afterEach(() => db.afterEach()); test('Alice sees her document and not Bobs', async () => { db.setContext({ role: 'authenticated', 'jwt.claims.user_id': 'aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa' }); const result = await db.query( 'SELECT id FROM app.documents ORDER BY id' ); expect(result.rows).toEqual([{ id: 101 }]); }); The query has no ownership filter. The policy must make Alice’s document visible and keep Bob’s out of the result. setContext() applies the role and identity settings through SET LOCAL and set_config(..., true) , scoping them to the transaction. They supply the identity the policies read. Nothing validates a token. Test identities must match what the application’s policies expect. The RLS tutorial covers the setup. The harness seeds through pgsql-seed , which loads SQL files, programmatic fixtures, CSV, JSON, or migrations. One harness, many platforms The same harness runs under other stacks: supabase-test supplies Supabase roles, schemas, and authentication defaults. drizzle-orm-test runs Drizzle queries within the managed transaction. pglite-test uses in-process PGlite, with no external database service when the schema and required extensions are supported. graphile-test runs GraphQL against a PostGraphile schema backed by the test database. graphile-realtime-test adds subscription testing. In one supabase-test run, noted by Supabase CEO Paul Copplestone , 246 tests across 44 databases completed in four seconds. Scaffolding the loop with pgpm pgpm , Constructive’s package manager for modular PostgreSQL, scaffolds workspaces with pgsql-test , Jest, and GitHub Actions; getConnections() deploys the module’s plan by default. Start with pgpm init workspace , then add a schema change and a test. Each change ships deploy , verify , and revert scripts. verify checks that the schema landed. The tests check that it behaves. The scaffolded workspace extends the same feedback loop into CI with safegres . Tests verify that database behavior is correct, and safegres checks the deployed schema for security and performance regressions. Its CI job enforces a security threshold and compares performance findings against a committed baseline, so a change cannot lower the schema’s security grade or add performance findings. Postgres enforces the rules. pgsql-test brings verification of those rules into the application development loop. Availability pgsql-test and its integrations are MIT licensed and available on npm and PyPI . Get started: Tutorials · End-to-end testing course · npm · Source code

article.title: Where Rust actually is in Windows 11
article.summary: Two Windows recovery and deployment DLLs were already shipping Rust in the original 24H2 build, and on this machine Microsoft’s own symbol files attribute 96.6 and 96.2 percent of their code to rustc. Neither appears in any Rust-in-Windows write-up I could find.
article.dek: Two Windows recovery and deployment DLLs were already shipping Rust in the original 24H2 build, and on this machine Microsoft’s own symbol files attribute 96.6 and 96.2 percent of their code to rustc.
article.hook: Two Windows recovery and deployment DLLs were already shipping Rust in the original 24H2 build, and on this machine Microsoft’s own symbol files attribute 96.6 and 96.2 percent of their code to rustc.

sections.heading: Context: what is changing
sections.body: Two Windows recovery and deployment DLLs were already shipping Rust in the original 24H2 build, and on this machine Microsoft’s own symbol files attribute 96.6 and 96.2 percent of their code to rustc. Neither appears in any Rust-in-Windows write-up I could find. The components everyone does name, the GDI kernel driver, sudo, DirectWrite, were announced years ago; what was missing was a measurement. So this is a census of one Windows 11 25H2 installation, 13,988 live files and 44,889 more in the component store, with every Rust marker classified by hand and the linker’s own records used to count how many bytes of each binary rustc actually produced.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: The public record is thinner than the discourse. At BlueHat IL in March 2023, David Weston said Windows would probably be booting with Rust in the kernel within several weeks or months. The Register’s April 2023 report of that talk put numbers on it: DWriteCore, the DirectWrite implementation in the Windows App SDK, at about 152,000 lines of Rust alongside 96,000 of C++, and the Win32 GDI port at 36,000 lines, booting but disabled behind a feature flag. In July 2023, Insider build 25905 shipped a kernel driver called win32kbase_rs.sys , which Microsoft described as a new implementation of GDI region and a small trial . In February 2024, Sudo for Windows arrived as an open-source Rust project.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: The toolchain has a public record too, and it is easy to miss. A September 2024 issue in an unrelated Microsoft repository names msrustup and the Microsoft Rust toolchain in passing, so the existence of an internal distribution has been visible for two years. Then, a week after the census below was taken, Microsoft described it properly: on 10 September 2026 Victor Ciura published a Rust Foundation guest post announcing Rust as a Tier-1 language at Microsoft and naming rustc_codegen_utc , an alternative rustc code generation backend in the same architectural family as rustc_codegen_llvm that wires the Rust compiler into MSVC’s own UTC backend. It has been self-hosted since Rust 1.90, is used in more than a hundred Microsoft repositories, and is credited with cross-language inlining and hotpatch support. That post describes in the abstract a good deal of what the binaries below show concretely. Section 9 is where the two meet.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now
sections.body: The important part is whether this change carries beyond the headline and becomes tangible in real product use. Updates like this often look small at first but end up changing everyday product behavior.

sections.heading: What to watch next
sections.body: What matters next is rollout pace, regional limits, and whether daily behavior actually changes.

draft_context.source_title: Anthropic-linked CVEs pile up, attackers mostly shrug
draft_context.description: Despite the concern that advanced AI models’ bug-hunting prowess will lead to attackers exploiting more newly uncovered CVEs, fewer than 0.5 percent of the vulnerabilities linked to Anthropic or Project Glasswing are being batttered in the wild, according to VulnCheck security researcher Patrick Garrity. Garrity began tracking CVEs attributed to Project Glasswing, Anthropic’s initiative to give select partners access to its Claude Mythos Preview model, shortly after the AI company announced the program in April. At the time, Anthropic said the new model was too risky to release publicly because its bug-finding and exploitation skills surpass all but the most skilled humans. As such, Anthropic restricted access to Mythos Preview to vetted Glasswing participants, who use the model for defensive security work, including finding and fixing flaws in their own software products and open source dependencies. Garrity’s Anthropic CVE tracker maintains a list of vulnerabilities credited to the Anthropic team and/or Project Glasswing and also checks these CVEs against the company's known exploited vulnerabilities index "to get a better read on the real Glasswing ‘danger factor.’" As of Monday, the CVE count is 225, and just one, a critical SQL injection bug in Ghost (CVE-2026-26980), has been exploited in the wild. “There's a big difference between finding vulnerabilities and whether they're actually useful to and will be used by threat actors,” Garrity told The Register. “The main thing this data highlights is that what Anthropic is discovering and disclosing is fairly limited in impact, and from what we can tell, isn't resulting in different outcomes from a threat perspective than a random selection of other vulnerabilities would.” Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to our questions, but we will update this story if we hear back. Garrity says he doesn’t dispute AI’s ability to find bugs. Indeed, anyone following security disclosures over the past few months would have a hard time arguing that AI models aren’t bringing to light significantly more security flaws than ever before. Case in point: recent massive patch drops from Microsoft, Apple, Palo Alto Networks, and don’t even get us started on open source projects. Also, as Garrity pointed out, these vulnerability-finding skills aren’t “a capability unique to one model or harness.” “A lot of the hysteria we're seeing assumes that every vulnerability or bug is likely to be used by threat actors,” he told The Register. “But the reality is that only a small fraction ever get used in exploitation campaigns. Historically, that's ranged from just under one percent to two percent of vulnerabilities that get weaponized and used in the wild.” Plus, while recent AI models excel at finding bugs, they still aren’t great at fixing them, as a couple of recent studies have highlighted. In one of these, 1Password’s research team produced and analyzed 6,080 patches developed by two frontier models: OpenAI's ChatGPT-5.5 and Anthropic's Opus 4.8. The models generated fixes that fully resolved the vulnerability just 26 percent of the time, while about 54 percent either failed to resolve the vulnerability, introduced a new vulnerability, or did both. Another study by app security shop Veracode found that across more than 100 models and 80 coding tasks, the average security pass rate for AI-generated code was just 56 percent. This all means that the work involved in developing and applying security fixes still requires humans. “The bar for vulnerability discovery is much lower with AI, but the real gap lies downstream in coordination, triage, remediation, and patch deployment, which is still largely people-intensive work, as Anthropic itself has acknowledged,” Garrity said. “It appears they might not have realized this until after they launched the project.”®

paragraphs: Theo dõi mắt là tính năng hoạt động trên iPhone 12 và iOS 18 trở về sau

Được giới thiệu lần đầu tiên trên iOS 18, tính năng Theo dõi mắt hoạt động trên các mẫu iPhone 12 trở lên. Nó được phát triển đặc biệt để hỗ trợ người dùng khuyết tật về thể chất, giúp họ sử dụng thiết bị một cách rảnh tay mà không cần đến phụ kiện bên ngoài. Tuy nhiên, người dùng bình thường cũng có thể khai thác cách điều khiển iPhone như vậy để thay đổi trải nghiệm tương tác với thiết bị.

Theo mặc định, đây là tính năng bị tắt. Để kích hoạt, người dùng cần đặt iPhone ở vị trí ổn định, đảm bảo đủ ánh sáng và khoảng cách giữa khuôn mặt và camera khoảng 30 cm. Sau đó, hãy làm theo các bước sau:

Sau khi hoàn tất hiệu chỉnh, người dùng có thể thêm các điều khiển "Giữ lâu" và "Cuộn" vào Menu AssistiveTouch. Từ đó, AssistiveTouch sẽ xuất hiện trên màn hình, cho phép người dùng dễ dàng điều khiển các chức năng như cuộn, quay lại màn hình chính hay mở Trung tâm điều khiển.
Trải nghiệm với các tính năng cơ bản khá tốt, nhưng các thao tác nâng cao hơn chưa thực sự ấn tượng

Mặc dù tính năng Theo dõi mắt trên lý thuyết rất hữu ích, nhưng thực tế lại có những hạn chế. Qua thử nghiệm trên iPhone 16 Pro Max với iOS 26 , người viết nhận thấy tính năng này hoạt động khá tốt trong việc điều hướng cơ bản. Con trỏ theo dõi mắt có thể dễ dàng bám vào các biểu tượng ứng dụng và tùy chọn menu. Tuy nhiên, việc sử dụng tính năng này để gõ chữ lại gặp nhiều khó khăn. Con trỏ thường không tự động bám vào các phím ở rìa bàn phím, gây khó khăn trong việc nhập liệu.

article.title: Mã độc Android mới tích hợp AI để đánh cắp tài khoản ngân hàng và mã PIN
article.summary: Các nhà nghiên cứu tại zLabs thuộc hãng bảo mật Zimperium vừa phân tích một trojan mới trên Android mang tên RatHat với quy trình lây nhiễm tự động và phức tạp. Điểm mới nguy hiểm của mã độc này là trao quyền truy cập cây trợ năng cho một trợ lý AI trực tiếp để tự động quyết định thao tác chạm hoặc cuộn màn hình, thay vì tuân theo các kịch bản lập trình sẵn cố định.

sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: Mã độc Android RatHat ứng dụng AI để đánh cắp thông tin nhạy cảm.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Nạn nhân thường bị lừa cài đặt tệp APK độc hại qua tin nhắn giả mạo hoặc quảng cáo dẫn đến trang tải ngụy trang trình duyệt Chrome hay ứng dụng xem phim, sau đó bị ép cấp quyền dịch vụ trợ năng (Accessibility). Lợi dụng quyền này, RatHat âm thầm tự kích hoạt tính năng Wireless Debugging và đọc mã xác thực trên màn hình để thiết lập phiên Android Debug Bridge (ADB), giúp mã độc mở đường hầm vượt tường lửa mà không cần máy tính hỗ trợ.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Để chiếm đoạt tài khoản, RatHat tạo ra một màn hình giả mạo phủ trên các ứng dụng tài chính nhằm đánh cắp thông tin đăng nhập, mã OTP và mã xác thực đa yếu tố. Đáng chú ý, mã độc còn sở hữu khả năng ghi lại trực tiếp tọa độ ngón tay chạm trên màn hình từ trình điều khiển nhập liệu, rồi đối chiếu với cơ sở dữ liệu bố cục bàn phím để giải mã chính xác mã PIN và hình vẽ mở khóa, vô hiệu hóa hoàn toàn cơ chế chống đọc trộm màn hình.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Bên cạnh khả năng chặn tin nhắn SMS và trao quyền điều khiển thiết bị bán tự động cho AI, đường dẫn tấn công biến thiên của RatHat còn khiến các công cụ bảo mật di động truyền thống khó phát hiện. Thậm chí, trojan này còn có khả năng tự động khôi phục lại ứng dụng độc hại sau khi người dùng gỡ cài đặt nhờ một chương trình chạy ngầm ẩn giấu trong hệ thống.

Bên cạnh khả năng chặn tin nhắn SMS và trao quyền điều khiển thiết bị bán tự động cho AI, đường dẫn tấn công biến thiên của RatHat còn khiến các công cụ bảo mật di động truyền thống khó phát hiện. Thậm chí, trojan này còn có khả năng tự động khôi phục lại ứng dụng độc hại sau khi người dùng gỡ cài đặt nhờ một chương trình chạy ngầm ẩn giấu trong hệ thống.

Để phòng tránh, người dùng tuyệt đối không bật Developer Options, từ chối cấp quyền trợ năng bất thường và chỉ nên cài đặt ứng dụng từ kho chính thức như Google Play hoặc sử dụng chế độ Advanced Protection của Android.

draft_context.source_title: Sonos Ace Ultra review: more musical, more feature-rich, much improved headphones
draft_context.description: Sonos Ace Ultra: two-minute review Sonos is making a real statement of intent with its new wireless headphones, the Sonos Ace Ultra. The multi-room master has made a whole host of improvements to this upgraded wireless over-ear model, which has arrived two years after the original Ace came to market. The Sonos Ace Ultra have enhanced custom 40mm drivers, a new headphone engine, better battery life, better noise-cancelling, and more detailed EQ to name a few things. So can they finally compete with flagship rivals from the likes of Sony and Bose to become some of the best noise-cancelling headphones we've tested ? Here’s what I think after weeks of testing. Let’s start by addressing the most important area of all: sound quality. We felt that the original Ace fell short of the best headphones around due to one main issue: their middling musicality. But the Ace Ultra have remedied that, and then some. When listening to the Sonos Ace Ultra beside the original model, the differences were stark. Where the standard Sonos Ace sounded confined, overstretched, and unrefined, the Ace Ultra offered openness, intricate detailing, and a broader, more organized soundstage. What’s more, they provide better balance across the frequency range, with deep yet controlled bass, rich but less overzealous mids, and tight, articulate treble. While I still consider some similarly priced competitors, like the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3 to supply slightly more premium, detailed sound (for music, that is), the Ace Ultra are really not far behind. Sonos listened to the critics, and proved that it's up to the task of going toe-to-toe with the titans of the headphone world. We already loved the original Ace for movies, though, finding that they offered immersive Dolby Atmos audio with effective head-tracking to boot. And that’s much the same on the Ace Ultra. They whip up wonderful width, strong command over height effects, and never neglect the fundamentals like clear dialogue and cinematic, pounding bass. But what’s new on the Ace Ultra? Although music got a seismic upgrade, other alterations feel a bit more incremental — but that’s by no means a bad thing. Two more microphones have been added to the Ultra, bringing the total to ten, and ANC is great here. Wherever I was, my soundings were subdued to great effect, almost creating a bubble of silence. ANC is adaptive this time around and adjusts nicely, and the transparency mode works a treat. Call quality is strong too, as you may expect. Battery life has also seen a boost, and you’ll now get up to 35 hours with ANC on. Is this anything groundbreaking? No. But it’s slightly above the 30-hour standard for headphones in this price bracket, and I never felt that I had to charge these cans very regularly. The battery is also replaceable, and a rapid charging mode means you can get three hours of playback if you spend three minutes juicing them up. EQ options have also been expanded beyond the basic two-band equalizer found on the standard Ace headphones. There’s an eight-band option now as well as adaptive EQ, meaning you can genuinely tailor sound to your specific tastes. We also need to talk about the Wi-Fi capabilities of the Sonos Ace Ultra. No, we’re still not at the point where we can directly stream tunes over a local internet connection, but there are some nifty features at play. First of all, TV Audio Swap is back, enabling you to link the headphones to a compatible Sonos soundbar, and transfer sound seamlessly. This is highly responsive and effective, and while I didn’t find myself using this feature a ton, you can avoid the latency issues you’d get from connecting headphones to your TV over Bluetooth. The Ace Ultra also add Headphone Linking, though, which means you can also transfer sound from compatible speakers, like the Sonos Play, for instance. This is equally reliable as TV Audio Swap, and is a great option if you’re listening to music at home but want to keep listening without distracting others. It’s clear to see that the Sonos Ace Ultra don’t look very different from the previous model, but that’s no bad thing. They’re sleek, well-built, and offer a neat combination of comfort and over-ear security. They’re not fully foldable, and the included case could be better quality-wise, but these are fairly minor pain points in the grand scheme of things. Considering that the Ace Ultra cost the same as the original Ace at the point of launch — and actually less in the UK — they feel like a much more worthwhile investment. They’re by no means cheap, but their enhancements are meaningful and substantial, making these a great pair of headphones whether you have a pre-existing Sonos system or not. As a result, these are a great pair of headphones for music and movie lovers alike that feel worth the outlay — and are easy to recommend if you want a great all-round pair of premium wireless headphones. (Image credit: Future) Sonos Ace Ultra review: price & release date Priced at $449 / £399 / AU$699 First released September 2026 The Sonos Ace Ultra were released in September 2026, about two years after the original Sonos Ace headphones. The new model is priced at $449 / £399 / AU$699, which is the same as the standard Ace cost at launch in the US and Australia, though they’re actually cheaper in the UK than the original Ace were at the point of release. Given their price, the Ace Ultra have some extremely hot competition. For example, the Sony WH-1000XM6 are similarly priced, and offer an incredible mix of balanced, dynamic, and impactful sound alongside some of the best noise-cancelling on the market and a giant suite of features. Other competitors include the noise-crushing Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones Gen 2 , the spacious sounding Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3 , and the ultra-detailed Sennheiser HDB 630 . Sonos Ace Ultra review: specs Drivers Next-gen 40mm custom Active noise cancellation Yes Battery life 35 hours (ANC on) Weight 0.7lbs / 322g Connectivity Bluetooth 6.0, USB-C Frequency range 20Hz-20kHz (Image credit: Future) Sonos Ace Ultra review: features Excellent ANC with adaptive mode and effective transparency option Higher-res audio available as well as Dolby Atmos for spatial sound TV Audio Swap and Headphone Linking works very well The Sonos Ace Ultra boast an excellent suite of features and are a highly personalizable, smart set of headphones. Let’s kick off with ANC, which has had quite the revamp. Now, you can toggle on an adaptive mode, which adjusts for things like fit, whether you’re wearing glasses, and if you make sudden head movements. But that’s not all. Sonos has also boosted the number of mics for the Ultra, with ten to the original Ace’s eight. The mics can monitor your surroundings and cut out external noise in real time, and they do this to great effect. Yes, the Ace Ultra supply great ANC, and no matter my environment, I was treated to satisfying, distraction-free listening. When out on walks, the sounds of cars passing by were totally nullified. When typing away in the office, the clacking of keyboards was fully subdued, and when travelling on public transport, engine sounds and surrounding chatter were put right to the sword. The Aware Mode is also very effective, and makes it incredibly easy to tune into your surroundings, with the new Voice Boost mode able to improve the clarity of voices around you if you toggle it on. The upgraded microphone system also helps the Ace Ultra to handle phone calls with greater care than ever before. When taking calls when out and about, my speech was perfectly comprehensible, and never sounded obscured by background noise, even when walking in a busy part of my city. Something else that’s received a boost is battery life. Sonos says that the Ace Ultra are capable of staying alive for 35 hours on a single charge, and my testing found this to be pretty accurate. This is a slight improvement on the original Ace, which could deliver 30 hours of use, which is essentially the standard for headphones in this price category. There’s also a rapid charging option, which gives the Ace Ultra three hours of playback from a three minute charge and a power saving mode if you want to extend the headphones’ life in a pinch. One of the more welcome additions to the Ace Ultra is their expanded EQ options. Now, you can make use of an eight-band equalizer to customize the sound of the headphones to your specific taste. This is a big improvement on the basic two-band equalizer on the original Ace (for bass and treble levels), though there’s a more basic three-band option on the Ace Ultra if you prefer a less detail-oriented approach. Let’s stick with sound, because there are a number of great features here that help you get the best out of both music and movies. First of all, you get all the hi-res goodness from the original Ace, with aptX codec support, as well as lossless audio via USB-C — and there’s a USB-C to 3.5mm cable bundled if you want to use them with a laptop, DJ controller, or other source device. Dolby Atmos also returns on the Ace Ultra, enabling you to enjoy spatial audio on the go. Once again, this works an absolute treat — especially for movies, where head-tracking also helps to further immerse you in on-screen action. I tried using the TV Audio Swap feature, which enabled me to connect the headphones to the Sonos Beam Ultra, and Atmos movies sounded wonderful — more on that in the ‘sound quality’ section. While the situations in which I’d use TV Audio Swap are admittedly niche, it's a very reliable feature. It harnesses Wi-Fi connectivity, so you don’t have to deal with the latency issues that connecting headphones to your TV over Bluetooth would bring. And you can easily switch between the soundbar, headphones, and other compatible Sonos speakers with a simple press of a button, which is highly convenient. The Ace Ultra’s new Headphone Engine 2 also enables Headphone Linking, which allows them to directly connect to other components in your Sonos system — including compatible speakers such as the Sonos play — and move audio to and from your speakers and headphones. Like TV Audio Swap, this feels seamless and speedy to activate, and is great if you’re blasting music at home, but don’t want to disturb others if they want some peace and quiet. On top of all of this, you get the usual good stuff: multi-point pairing, Bluetooth 6.0 connectivity, wear detection, and a relatively intuitive companion app. And when you add all of this together, I think it's fair to say that the Ace Ultra offer an incredibly fleshed-out, and well-refined feature set. Features score: 5/5 (Image credit: Future) Sonos Ace Ultra review: sound quality Big improvement over original Ace with better soundstaging, detailing, and control Deep, immersive bass, clean mids, and tight, expressive treble Fantastic Dolby Atmos performance While we considered the original Sonos Ace to be a good pair of headphones, their somewhat middling musicality ended up holding them back from greatness. But luckily, Sonos has listened to the criticism, implemented next-gen 40mm custom drivers, and remedied a lot of the issues we had with the previous model. The result? A genuinely great-sounding pair of headphones. I tried comparing the Sonos Ace Ultra against the original model directly, and when I say that the difference is striking, I truly mean it. In essence, the Ace Ultra provide a significantly broader soundstage with far better organization and balance, as well as deeper, more controlled bass, and more articulate, detailed treble. I also found them to offer superior handling of dynamics and enhanced instrument separation, meaning that, for me, Sonos is closer to rivals like Bose and Sony than ever before. Sonos has been keen to talk up the Ace Ultra’s improved bass, so I started out by listening to a house track, Get It On by Jansons. The Ace Ultra delivered palpable, pumping bass, that was rhythmic and rapid, never sounding lethargic or boomy. This never concealed other sounds across the frequency range, either, with synths in the mid-range sounding well defined and tonally accurate, and high-pitched drums coming through with precision and vigor, helping the track to maintain its high energy. Treble was especially tighter on the Ace Ultra compared to the original model, and the wider soundstage gave each individual element more room to breathe, and this became a theme across all of my listening tests. For instance, with the funk track Joía Rara by Brylho, the upgrade the Ultra provided was considerable. On the original Sonos Ace, the soundstage felt confined, with guitars lacking definition in the mix, and as the track built, the horns, bass, vocals, and guitars sounded slightly convoluted, resulting in a messier presentation than I’d expected. But on the Ace Ultra, things were totally different. Guitars in the intro occupied a unique pocket, bass was well-balanced, and finer percussive details were perfectly audible. Vocals were also separated to greater effect, and while they weren’t the most textured or forward, they were more than clear enough. Are the Sonos Ace Ultra the best-sounding headphones in their price bracket? Well, they’re not far behind the competition, though I do still think a couple of models edge just ahead. For example, I tested them side by side with the Sony WH-1000XM6 , and I found that Sony’s cans supplied a slightly more dynamic low-end output and detailing in the mid-range. It was very close between these two, though. Of course, if you want the most expansive soundstage, headphones like the AirPods Max 2 will edge out the Ace Ultra, but they’re slightly more expensive. Before we move onto design, we have to talk about the Ace Ultra’s handling of spatial audio. They support Dolby Atmos as well as head tracking, really helping you to immerse yourself in your favorite movies and TV shows, and the expansiveness that the headphones supply is seriously impressive. When using TV Audio Swap with some 4K UHD Blu-ray discs, the Ace Ultra were able to conjure up an excellent sense of width, almost like some of the best Dolby Atmos soundbars can. I started by watching Elio , and the Ace Ultra did an incredible job — voices were clear, and as characters moved across the screen, they were tracked with precision, and if I tilted my head, sound shifted dynamically as if I was speaking with characters directly. As Elio returned to earth, deep, pounding bass hit with immense power too, but didn’t sound muddy or overbearing. With Godzilla Minus One , the sense of a plane flying overhead in the opening scene was captured far more effectively than expected. It was genuinely convincing, as if the sound was truly coming from above. Dialogue was clear again, and Godzilla’s almighty screech was both tonally accurate and controlled, rather than tinny. More generally, the movie’s action scenes had tremendous width, creating a genuinely immersive experience. Sound quality score: 4.5/5 (Image credit: Future) Sonos Ace Ultra review: design Beautiful design, and very well made Comfortable yet secure fit Not fully foldable, but case included for added security The Ace Ultra look an awful lot like the original Ace, but as someone who loved the way those headphones looked, that’s a big plus. The ear cups are relatively flat and understated, the rounded look is sleek and sexy, and the metallic details only add to the sense of premium. The button controls have shifted about slightly, but they’re incredibly easy to reach, and are all very responsive. I tried the Soft White version which is stylish and modern, but the Ace Ultra are also available in Black, Agave, and Sand. All of these colorways are minimalistic and suit the luxurious vibe of the headphones to perfection. In terms of fit, the Ace Ultra strike a really strong balance between comfort and security — they’re the goldilocks of headphones, if you will. There’s enough clamping power to prevent excess sound seeping in and keep them on your head during a workout or similar, but I never found this to be overbearing. Even when I was wearing a hat, the Ace Ultra felt really snug, with the plush ear cups and padded headband helping me to enjoy my music for many hours on end. One subtle thing I like is how the inside of the right ear cup is green, making it easy to know which side is which when throwing the cans on. The right cup also features a slider, which can be used to easily adjust volume or trigger the Audio Swap feature. I usually prefer touch controls, but the tactile and reliable nature of these buttons might just have converted me. Something that may frustrated a few users is that the Ace Ultra are not foldable. Yes, the ear cups rotate flat for when you want to stow the headphones in the case, but rivals like the Sony WH-1000XM6 offer a more compact, travel-friendly design. In addition, the case itself doesn’t quite offer the quality I was expecting, with a fuzzy exterior that’s a bit prone to picking up fibers. I also found that the zip jammed a bit easily. I much prefer the magnetic case of the XM6, which is more seamless to use and has a more quality look and feel. Design score: 4.5/5 (Image credit: Future) Sonos Ace Ultra review: value More fully featured and better sounding than the original Ace… …but for the same price (at the point of launch) A worthwhile choice for those with or without a pre-existing Sonos system The Sonos Ace Ultra cured the single ailment that plagued the original model above else: their middling musicality. When I tested both headphones side by side, the difference was night and day. The original Ace were held back by a limited soundstage, underwhelming instrument separation, and a lack of balance across the frequency range. But the Ace Ultra sound so much more open, organized, and detailed, and truly compete with flagship rivals from Sony and Bose. On top of that, you’re getting excellent Dolby Atmos performance, Headphone Linking and TV Audio Swap for linking up to other Sonos products, a beautiful design, and strong noise-cancelling capabilities. Considering that the Sonos Ace Ultra cost the same as the original model did at the point of launch — and less than the standard Ace initially cost in the UK — that’s pretty impressive. At $449 / £399 / AU$699, they’re still quite the investment, of course. And I do think that some rivals, including the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3 just edge above them in terms of sound quality. But those models can’t compete when it comes to movies — a big selling point of the Ace headphones. And the interactivity that these have with other Sonos products makes them a slam-dunk for owners of products like the Sonos Beam Ultra and Sonos Play. Even if you don’t have a Sonos system, these headphones still justify their price with great all-round performance, a delicious design, higher-res audio codecs and wired lossless sound, as well as solid battery life. All in all, then, the Ace Ultra feel like a much more worthwhile investment than the original Ace, and manage to earn their price. paragraphs: Last year, Peloton did a sweeping refresh of its hardware that added cameras, fans, and AI-powered software called Peloton IQ. This year, it’s zeroing in on its treadmill lineup — refreshing its two existing Treads and adding the new, more affordable Tread Flex into the fold.

At a New York City launch event, Peloton chief product officer Nick Caldwell told the press the $2,195 Flex — which can be folded upright to save 50 percent more floor space — was meant to address user feedback for a more easily stowed machine. When folded, the Flex purportedly has a smaller overall footprint than the Bike Plus. It also has caster wheels so it can be maneuvered more easily. For safety, the wheels can be locked in place, it has the existing Tread Lock passcode, and it has a slow-opening mechanism using a two-cylinder release. In person, it took about 25 seconds for the deck to lower fully. You don’t have to do anything or push the deck, and there’s no ka-thunk — it just sort of gently falls. That said, Peloton confirmed at the event that there are no sensor-based safety features.

While running, the Flex has a relatively quiet motor at 70 decibels. It’s hard to gauge exactly how quiet it is in a demo space, but it was notably quieter than other treadmills I’ve run on. I don’t think most people will have an issue running on the Flex’s shorter deck, but it might be a concern if you have particularly long legs. Like Peloton’s other treadmills, it has a swivel screen so you can do other types of workouts, but no camera, precluding it from some of the new Peloton IQ features (more on that below).

Meanwhile, its existing two treadmills have been rebranded as the $3,495 Tread Vision and $6,695 Tread Plus Vision. (The former is a $200 price increase, while the latter is the same price.) Here, the upgrades are more refinements. The Vision has a new deck that’s got better cushioning, redesigned jump buttons that let you go up and down for speed / incline, plus a redesigned tray for holding tablets, phones, and water bottles. The Tread Plus Vision also has the new jump buttons, plus a new “sled” mode that may appeal to Hyrox or Crossfit athletes. Both still have a swivel screen and motion tracking cameras that enable some new treadmill-related Peloton IQ features.

As far as software goes, all the treadmills are getting personalized pace. After about 10 running workouts, you’ll get a recommended pace targets that automatically populate within a workout. They may adjust over time as fitness improves. Peloton is also launching a new feature called ReRun, which lets you upload outdoor run course data recorded in the Peloton app or from a smartwatch into the treadmill so you can “re-run” them. That includes automatic incline adjustments based on outdoor elevation on a route. Peloton is partnering with NYRR so that users can “re-run” segments of the New York City Marathon course. At the event, press were told that the company is exploring partnerships for other famous races as well.

For the camera-enabled treadmills, Peloton is adding a running analysis feature. There’s a one-time calibration and then afterward, the movement-tracking camera will run in the background of subsequent workouts. Based on steps, cadence, vertical oscillation, and stride length, users will get a running efficiency score and tips on how to improve their form.

draft_context.source_title: Want your laptop battery to last for years? Avoid these 9 mistakes
draft_context.description: One of the most frustrating aspects of an aging laptop is how the battery life diminishes. Even super-long-lasting laptops eventually decay, and what once lasted a full day starts needing a charge before the work day ends. Before long, you’re using it plugged in all the time. But it doesn’t have to be this way! Modern laptops are designed to be efficient, long-lasting machines. If you treat them right and take good care of them, you can make sure the battery maintains its longevity for much longer—at least a few extra years. And if you don’t take good care of it? Well, expect the battery to lose capacity much sooner than you’d like. Here are some of the best habits you should practice if you want your laptop battery to truly last several years. (Not sure if your laptop battery is still good? Use this free tool to check it right now! ) Limit your battery’s max charge to 80% It might sound counterintuitive to reduce your overall battery capacity in order to get more out of it, but it’s true: keeping your battery at 100% for extended periods can accelerate wear and tear. That’s why you shouldn’t leave your laptop plugged in . Maxing out at around 80% reduces stress on the battery and slows its capacity loss over time. You’ll get less runtime per charge, but you’ll be able to enjoy that 80% capacity for much longer this way. (And if you won’t be using it for a long time, make sure it’s at 50% before storing it away.) Panos Sakalakis / Unsplash While Apple has a built-in feature on MacBooks for restricting max battery percentage, there’s no OS-specific solution for Windows 11. However, you might find such a setting in your laptop’s BIOS or your manufacturer’s specific utility app. The big-name brands—including Dell, Lenovo, HP, and Asus—usually offer a battery limiting feature. For older laptops, or ones that lack this feature for whatever reason, you’ll have to manually unplug your laptop from its charger whenever it reaches the desired charge capacity. Don’t let your battery hit 0% When a lithium-ion battery runs completely empty—and pretty much all laptops use lithium-ion batteries—the internal chemistry of the battery can become unstable. Long story short, draining a laptop battery to 0% can cause permanent wear and tear on the battery itself, impacting its ability to hold a charge and reducing its overall charge capacity. Make sure to recharge your laptop once it hits around 20% if you want to keep the battery healthy. At worst, don’t let it drop below 10%. Watch your laptop’s temperature Batteries have safe operating temperatures and you should do your best to keep them within that range. If you leave your laptop in the sun or in a hot car, you risk temperatures rising above that, which can accelerate wear and tear on the battery cells. In the worst extreme, it can even cause the battery to swell and risk catching fire. (At that point, you should immediately dispose of it because it’s a real hazard.) amt8u / Unsplash Don’t leave your laptop in your car or outside over night, either. Cold temperatures slow down the chemical reactions in lithium-ion batteries, potentially leading to reduced charge capacity. If you try to use the laptop while it’s super cold, that can also cause permanent damage to the battery cells. If your laptop ever gets particularly cold, let it warm up to room temperature before turning it on. Keeping the laptop at comfortable operating temperatures is a good idea in general, as an overheating laptop will reduce performance and system stability. Learn more about what to do if your laptop is overheating all the time . Keep it plugged in while gaming Modern laptops are designed to draw power from the outlet when plugged in, so if you’re going to be sitting at a desk for an extended time doing something intense—like gaming—then it makes sense to plug in. Thiago Trevisan / IDG By plugging in, you’ll get the full power of the laptop’s gaming ability (since they usually throttle, even if only partially, when running off battery power) and you’ll help preserve your battery’s lifespan by not putting it through constant drain-recharge cycles. In fact, if you’re gaming a lot, there’s a lot more you can do to keep your battery going strong for years. See our collection of tips for extending your gaming laptop’s battery life . Keep it clean and clear FeriDhaniHasri / Shutterstock If your laptop’s vents are dusty or dirty, its cooling can be affected. A hot laptop works harder to achieve the same performance, and the battery life will suffer in turn. Make sure to clean your laptop every few months to keep it in peak condition and prevent undue battery wear. Make sure you aren’t using it somewhere that’s blocking the vents, too. Soft blankets, sofas, cushions, and pillows are terrible surfaces for laptop use because they’re soft and comfort to the laptop, blocking vents and causing heat buildup. Hard surfaces allow for clear airflow and can make a big difference to laptop cooling, thus extending battery life. Optimize your power settings Windows 11 has a number of useful settings you can manage to improve battery life and help it last longer over the lifespan of your device. If you can get the battery to last longer on an individual charge, you’ll recharge it less often—and that’ll reduce wear on the battery over time. Jon Martindale / Foundry Navigate to Start > Settings > System > Power and battery > Screen and sleep to adjust how quickly your laptop goes into sleep mode and turns off its screen when on battery. If you leave your laptop idling a lot, cutting this down to just a few minutes can really help. If you want to extend your battery life temporarily, or once you pass a certain battery threshold, switch on Energy Saving Mode. Navigate to Start > Settings > System > Power and battery to turn it on or modify its settings. This’ll reduce performance, though, so only toggle this on if you really need it and don’t mind the sacrifice. You can also set it to “Balanced” or “Power Saver” power modes if you don’t need high-end gaming performance all the time. Navigate to Control Panel > System and Security > Power options and select the power plan that’s right for your needs. Tweak your screen Your laptop screen draws a lot of power, so adjusting its settings can impact your battery life. If you aren’t in a bright environment, lowering the screen brightness can go a long way to improving battery life. Your laptop should have keyboard shortcuts for this. Jon Martindale / Foundry You can also tweak the refresh rate. If you aren’t gaming, you don’t really need a 240Hz refresh rate (even if it does make your mouse pointer move more smoothly over the desktop and windows). Navigate to Settings > Display > Advanced Display to manually change your refresh rate to something lower. Alternatively, set it to Dynamic and your laptop will change the refresh rate as needed. Shut down background apps Unnecessary background apps will drain your battery life, and often you don’t need them running in the first place. Navigate to Start > Settings > System > Power and battery > Battery usage . Under Battery usage per app , you’ll be able to see which of your apps use the most power in the background. You can close them down, or stop them starting up with Windows entirely, to help extend your battery life and therefore boost your laptop’s overall battery longevity. Don’t forget to stay up-to-date Operating system and firmware updates aren’t going to magically make your laptop battery life longer, but Microsoft and laptop manufacturers do release efficiency and performance improvements sometimes. Making sure you’re fully up-to-date means your laptop is running as well as it can, and that’ll help your battery last longer. Further reading: Common mistakes that are killing your laptop

article.title: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You
article.summary: For one, AI is not trained on what it means for code to be maintainable. For instance, any reinforcement learning done needs a reward signal that can be measured immediately, not in months or years.

sections.body: For one, AI is not trained on what it means for code to be maintainable. For instance, any reinforcement learning done needs a reward signal that can be measured immediately, not in months or years. The AI learns rules from rulebooks meant for beginners. The AI notices patterns from code in the wild and let’s be honest, most code in the wild is pretty bad. There is no fitness function you can define for maintainable code, at least not one that we can discern, otherwise it would’ve been baked into our linters.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: Have you noticed how terrible is the AI at “simplifying” code? Yes, the SOTA models. It can’t even define functions properly, choosing to split functions into smaller functions that are not actually reusable. Extracting a smaller function from a bigger function is a very bad choice if, to understand the bigger function, you have to also read the implementation of the extracted smaller function. Defining reusable and clarifying functions is an art form, an art that takes mastery. Most developers, being still “advanced beginners” in the Dreyfus model , are not able to define good, clarifying, reusable functions and neither does the AI currently.

The “AI” industry has many flaws, the word “consent” being seemingly missing from training data and company handbooks is one of them. AI bros do not take “no” for an answer. When Apple advertised their deepfake feature back in June it became obvious Apple does not “think different.”

Digging through macOS 27 settings I turned off Siri (again). Of course, multiple unkillable Siri processes remain, stealing memory and writing data. For what purpose? Who knows. Note that they removed “Apple Intelligence” from this control.

Trawling the web I discovered Apple has hidden settings under “Screen Time” restrictions. This is supposed to be for parental controls. These settings don’t disable Apple “Intelligence” but they do clean up various menus by hiding the slop tools.
All of this garbage was enabled after upgrading to macOS 27 despite me having “Apple Intelligence & Siri” turned off already. That was a rather explicit “no”, no?

article.summary: SCMP đưa tin nhóm nghiên cứu đến từ Đại học Khoa học Kỹ thuật Điện tử Tây An, Đại học Thành phố Hong Kong và Đại học Phúc Đán phát triển phương pháp giúp một loại chip nhớ mới trở nên bền vững hơn hẳn, mở ra tiềm năng sử dụng trong máy tính hiệu suất cao và các hệ thống trí tuệ nhân tạo tương lai khi sự bùng nổ AI thúc đẩy nhu cầu về vật liệu bán dẫn tiên tiến hơn. sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: Nhóm nghiên cứu chứng minh vật liệu sắt điện cấu trúc wurtzite, loại vật liệu có khả năng chuyển đổi giữa hai trạng thái điện để lưu trữ dữ liệu, có thể trải qua hơn 10 tỷ chu kỳ ghi. Độ bền này cao gấp khoảng 100 lần so với mức đạt được trước đó, có thể thúc đẩy công nghệ bộ nhớ thế hệ mới. Đột phá trên hứa hẹn đưa bộ nhớ sắt điện tới gần ứng dụng thực tế trong phần cứng máy tính hơn. Đây là công nghệ bộ nhớ không bay hơi thử nghiệm, lưu trữ thông tin thông qua hướng phân cực điện bên trong vật liệu sắt điện cấu trúc wurtzite.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Theo NeoTeo , trong những năm gần đây, vật liệu sắt điện cấu trúc wurtzite (nhóm vật liệu bán dẫn có cấu trúc tinh thể lục phương) như nhôm scandium nitride (AlScN) thu hút nhiều sự chú ý với tiềm năng trở thành vật liệu bộ nhớ thế hệ mới do tốc độ chuyển đổi nhanh và mức tiêu thụ năng lượng thấp. AlScN cũng tương thích với những quy trình sản xuất bán dẫn hiện có, có thể đơn giản hóa quá trình tích hợp vào các thiết bị bộ nhớ tương lai.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Tuy nhiên, vật liệu này vấp phải một hạn chế đáng kể là bị xuống cấp sau khi chuyển đổi điện nhiều lần. Thiết bị AlScN hiện tại thường hỏng hóc sau khoảng 100 triệu chu kỳ ghi, kém xa so với yêu cầu hàng tỷ chu kỳ ghi của ứng dụng thương mại.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Các nhà nghiên cứu xác định sự tích tụ lỗ trống nitơ (những điểm thiếu nguyên tử nitơ) là lý do chính dẫn tới tỷ lệ hỏng hóc tương đối nhanh của chip nhớ sắt điện. Wang Ruiqing, nghiên cứu sinh tiến sĩ tại Đại học Khoa học Kỹ thuật Điện tử Tây An, một trong những tác giả của bài báo, giải thích: "Hãy tưởng tượng vật liệu sắt điện giống như một cánh đồng ngô được trồng gọn gàng, và lỗ trống nitơ đại diện cho chỗ thiếu cây giống". Các lỗ trống nitơ có thể di chuyển và tụ lại với nhau, cuối cùng hình thành đường dẫn qua vật liệu khiến điện rò rỉ và dẫn đến hỏng hóc.
